newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Bishop says Nobel Prize is for all Indonesians.
newsitem.headline: Bishop says Nobel Prize is for all Indonesians.

text.p: East Timor's Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Filipe Ximenes Belo, who jointly won the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize on Friday, said his award was a victory for all Indonesians.
"I see it as a victory for East Timorese...and all Indonesians," he told Reuters by telephone from Dili, the capital of the former Portuguese colony of East Timor.

The Nobel committee said Belo and East Timorese independence movement leader Jose Ramos Horta were awarded the prize for what it said were their efforts to bring peace to the troubled territory, invaded and annexed by Indonesia 20 years ago.
Belo said there was hard work ahead in the peace and reconciliation process. "Peace can be achieved through non-violent means," he said.
The victory placed a burden on his shoulders, he said, adding that he wished he had not won. He also said he hoped there would be no rejoicing in East Timor over his award but did not elaborate.
Belo, 51, was appointed bishop of East Timor in 1983. He has had to walk a thin line between the territory's Jakarta-appointed government and his increasingly frustrated flock.
